render.prompt:
Image 1 is a real phone photo of a room to edit. Image 2 is a placement guide: the same photo with numbered translucent boxes showing where each product goes; use it only for position and scale and never draw its boxes or numbers. Images 3 to 5 are the reference photos of products 1 to 3, in order.
1. Replace the rumpled gray duvet and pillow with product 1: White Textured Cotton Coverlet Set (bedding), real size 228 x 228 x 3 cm (width x depth x height). Dress the existing floor mattress along the right wall, pillows at the head near the window with duvet neatly folded. It belongs inside box 1 of the placement guide. Copy product 1 exactly from its reference photo: White crinkled cotton coverlet draped over a bed with two matching shams, lightweight textured weave and softly rumpled relaxed look. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
2. Add product 2: Striated Jute Area Rug (rug), real size 226.1 x 160 x 0.6 cm (width x depth x height). Centered on the wood floor between the bed and desk-wardrobe side, long edge parallel to bed, clear of doorway. It belongs inside box 2 of the placement guide. Copy product 2 exactly from its reference photo: Rectangular low-pile jute area rug in light beige linen with subtle horizontal striations and lightly textured woven surface. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
3. Add product 3: Abstract Pale Rose Framed Wall Art (wall art), real size 55.9 x 2.5 x 66 cm (width x depth x height). Hung on the right wall centered above the middle of the bed at eye height. It belongs inside box 3 of the placement guide. Copy product 3 exactly from its reference photo: Rectangular vertically oriented framed abstract painting with thick textured brushstrokes in pale pink, white and gray within a thin gold frame. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
Remove: stack of cardboard moving boxes. Show the floor and wall that were behind them, continuing the surrounding texture, so it looks like they were never there.
Hard rules: keep the exact same camera position, framing, lens distortion and perspective. Keep the walls, wallpaper, floor, ceiling, ceiling light, windows, blinds or curtains, doors and every object that is not listed exactly as they are. Keep the existing light direction, color temperature and exposure; new products receive the same light and cast soft, physically plausible contact shadows. The result must look like an unedited phone photo of the same room, not a render. Do not add anything else: no extra decor, no text, no numbers, no colored boxes or outlines.
